quests.instruction: Which activity is mainly practicing reading?
quests.correctAnswer: Following the words with your finger 📖
options: Counting out beads in groups of ten 🔢
Drawing and labeling a diagram of a flower 🌸
Following the words with your finger 📖
quests.hint: Look for the one that is about words on a page.
quests.explanation: Reading practice builds as you follow words, sound them out, and understand what they say.
quests.funFact: Pointing with a finger helps young readers keep their place.

quests.instruction: Why do students sometimes read aloud in class?
quests.correctAnswer: To practice reading smoothly and clearly 🗣️
options: To practice reading smoothly and clearly 🗣️
To make the classroom a little louder 📢
To find out who can read the fastest 🏁
quests.hint: Think about both reading and speaking.
quests.explanation: Reading aloud helps you practice saying words clearly and hearing how sentences sound.
quests.funFact: Reading aloud also lets your teacher hear which words are tricky.

quests.instruction: You come to a word you can't read. What is a good first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Sound it out one part at a time 🔤
options: Guess the word from the picture on the cover 📕
Sound it out one part at a time 🔤
Skip it and read the next page instead 📄
quests.hint: Break the word into small bits.
quests.explanation: Sounding out parts of the word helps you read new words yourself.
quests.funFact: Many long words are made from short parts you already know.

quests.instruction: Your teacher asks you to write a story. What should you do before you start?
quests.correctAnswer: Think of an idea and plan it 💡
options: Copy a friend's story ✏️
Think of an idea and plan it 💡
Write the last sentence first 🔚
quests.hint: Good writing starts with ideas.
quests.explanation: Planning your characters and what happens helps your story make sense.
quests.funFact: Many authors write notes before they start a story.

quests.instruction: Why do writers read through their first draft again?
quests.correctAnswer: To find mistakes and improve it 🔍
options: To make it shorter just because ✂️
To find mistakes and improve it 🔍
To copy someone else's ideas 👀
quests.hint: Think about making the writing better.
quests.explanation: Checking your draft helps you catch mistakes and make your ideas clearer.
quests.funFact: Professional writers often write several drafts of one piece.

quests.instruction: You are writing a letter to a friend. What do you put at the very beginning?
quests.correctAnswer: A greeting such as 'Dear Sam,' ✉️
options: A greeting such as 'Dear Sam,' ✉️
The date of your next birthday 🎂
Your goodbye 👋
quests.hint: Think of how a letter starts.
quests.explanation: A greeting shows who the letter is for and starts it politely.
quests.funFact: Letters usually end with a closing like 'Best wishes' and your name.

quests.instruction: Your class uses hand spans to measure the length of a desk. Which subject is this?
quests.correctAnswer: Math 🧮
options: Math 🧮
Music 🎵
Art 🎨
quests.hint: Think about measuring and numbers.
quests.explanation: Measuring and counting spans is a math activity, since you find out how long something is.
quests.funFact: A hand span is the distance from your thumb tip to your little finger tip.

quests.instruction: Your class makes a bar graph of everyone's favorite fruit. What are you learning?
quests.correctAnswer: How to show information in a chart 📊
options: How to paint a picture using fruit 🍎
How to show information in a chart 📊
How to write a poem about breakfast 📝
quests.hint: A graph turns numbers into a picture.
quests.explanation: A bar graph lets you compare amounts quickly, because taller bars mean more.
quests.funFact: A graph can show which fruit is the most popular in one look.

quests.instruction: Why do students practice counting, adding, and measuring in school?
quests.correctAnswer: To solve real-life problems with numbers 🔢
options: To learn to draw perfectly straight lines ✏️
To solve real-life problems with numbers 🔢
To make the homework longer each night 📚
quests.hint: Think about shops, cooking, and travel.
quests.explanation: Number skills help with shopping, telling time, and many other daily jobs.
quests.funFact: The word 'mathematics' comes from a Greek word meaning 'learning'.

quests.instruction: In a science experiment, you say what you think will happen before you try it. What is this called?
quests.correctAnswer: A prediction 🤔
options: A report card 📋
A conclusion 🏁
A prediction 🤔
quests.hint: It's a guess based on what you know.
quests.explanation: A prediction is what you think will happen before you test it, and then you check if you were right.
quests.funFact: Scientists often find that their predictions are wrong, and that can be useful.

quests.instruction: Why do scientists write down what they see during an experiment?
quests.correctAnswer: So they can check the results later 📝
options: So they can check the results later 📝
So they don't have to look again 👀
So the experiment lasts longer ⏳
quests.hint: Your memory can forget details.
quests.explanation: Notes keep exact details, so you can compare your results later.
quests.funFact: Notes and drawings are often called observations.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a science activity?
quests.correctAnswer: Measuring a bean plant each day 🌱
options: Writing a thank-you note to a guest ✉️
Singing a song with a group of friends 🎤
Measuring a bean plant each day 🌱
quests.hint: Think about observing and recording.
quests.explanation: Watching and measuring how a plant changes is a science activity, because you collect real evidence.
quests.funFact: A bean seed can sprout in about a week.

quests.instruction: Which art technique makes a picture from small pieces of paper stuck onto a page?
quests.correctAnswer: Collage 🖼️
options: Sketch ✏️
Collage 🖼️
Print 🖨️
quests.hint: You cut or tear, then glue.
quests.explanation: A collage is made by arranging cut or torn pieces of paper and gluing them down.
quests.funFact: The word 'collage' comes from a French word meaning 'to glue'.

quests.instruction: You want to add tiny details to a drawing. Which tool is best?
quests.correctAnswer: A fine-tip pencil ✏️
options: A fine-tip pencil ✏️
A big sponge 🧽
A wide paint roller 🖌️
quests.hint: Small details need a small point.
quests.explanation: A fine point gives you control to draw thin lines and small shapes.
quests.funFact: Artists often use different tools for outlines and for filling areas.

quests.instruction: Why might an artist step back and look at the drawing from far away?
quests.correctAnswer: To see the whole picture at once 👀
options: To make the paper look much bigger 📄
To help the paint dry a bit faster 💨
To see the whole picture at once 👀
quests.hint: Close up, you only see parts.
quests.explanation: Stepping back helps you check that the shapes and colors work together.
quests.funFact: From far away, you can see the overall shape and balance of a picture.

quests.instruction: Your teacher claps a pattern and you clap it back. What are you practicing?
quests.correctAnswer: Rhythm 🥁
options: Rhythm 🥁
Painting 🎨
Spelling 🔤
quests.hint: It's about beats and patterns.
quests.explanation: Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds in music.
quests.funFact: A metronome clicks at a steady speed to help musicians keep a beat.

quests.instruction: What is the word for how fast or slow music is?
quests.correctAnswer: Tempo ⏱️
options: Pitch 🎶
Tempo ⏱️
Volume 🔊
quests.hint: It's about speed.
quests.explanation: Tempo tells you how fast or slow to play or sing.
quests.funFact: The word 'tempo' comes from an Italian word meaning 'time'.

quests.instruction: A large group of people singing together is called what?
quests.correctAnswer: A choir 🎤
options: A choir 🎤
A band 🎸
An orchestra 🎻
quests.hint: They use their voices, not instruments.
quests.explanation: A choir sings together, often in different parts that blend.
quests.funFact: Many choirs split into higher and lower voices to make harmony.

quests.instruction: Why do you stretch gently after exercise?
quests.correctAnswer: To help your muscles relax and recover 🧘
options: To help your muscles relax and recover 🧘
To warm up before the game starts 🔥
To get your brain ready for a test 📝
quests.hint: Your muscles worked hard.
quests.explanation: Stretching after exercise helps your muscles relax and feel looser.
quests.funFact: Slow stretches work better than quick bouncing.

quests.instruction: What skill do team games help you practice?
quests.correctAnswer: Working together 🤝
options: Painting quietly 🎨
Spelling words 🔤
Working together 🤝
quests.hint: Think about how players depend on one another.
quests.explanation: Team games teach cooperation, listening, and playing fairly.
quests.funFact: Many team sports work best when every player has a different role.

quests.instruction: After running, your heart beats faster. What does this tell you?
quests.correctAnswer: Your body is working hard 💓
options: You must be sleepy 😴
You must be hungry 🍎
Your body is working hard 💓
quests.hint: Your heart pumps blood to your muscles.
quests.explanation: When you exercise, your heart beats faster to bring more oxygen to your muscles.
quests.funFact: Your heart is about as big as your fist.

quests.instruction: You typed a story and want to use it again tomorrow. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Save the file 💾
options: Restart the computer 🔄
Save the file 💾
Close it without saving ❌
quests.hint: Think about keeping your work.
quests.explanation: Saving stores your work, so it is still there when you come back.
quests.funFact: Many programs have an autosave feature, but saving yourself is still a good habit.

quests.instruction: You find a website for your project. What is a good thing to check?
quests.correctAnswer: Whether it comes from a trusted source 🔍
options: Whether it has lots of bright colors 🌈
Whether it's the first result 1️⃣
Whether it comes from a trusted source 🔍
quests.hint: Not everything online is correct.
quests.explanation: Checking where facts come from helps you know whether to trust them.
quests.funFact: Library books and school-approved sites are usually good sources.

quests.instruction: A pop-up asks for your name and home address. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Close it and tell your teacher 🙋
options: Type in your name and home address ⌨️
Ask a friend which details to enter ✋
Close it and tell your teacher 🙋
quests.hint: Personal information should stay private.
quests.explanation: Never share personal details online without a trusted adult's permission.
quests.funFact: Your full name, address, and phone number are private information.

quests.instruction: What is a school project?
quests.correctAnswer: A larger task on one topic over many lessons 📋
options: A single question that is part of a test ❓
A short game that the class plays at break 🎲
A larger task on one topic over many lessons 📋
quests.hint: It takes more than one lesson.
quests.explanation: Projects let you explore a topic in depth and often combine different skills.
quests.funFact: Projects can include writing, drawing, building, and presenting.

quests.instruction: What is a sensible first step for a project?
quests.correctAnswer: Choose your topic and make a plan 🗺️
options: Wait until the day before it is due ⏳
Choose your topic and make a plan 🗺️
Start gluing things right away 🧴
quests.hint: Plan before doing.
quests.explanation: A plan breaks the project into steps, so you know what to do and by when.
quests.funFact: Architects make detailed plans before any building is built.

quests.instruction: For a project about frogs, which source is most likely to give correct facts?
quests.correctAnswer: A library book about animals 📚
options: A library book about animals 📚
A rumor you heard in the hallway 🗣️
A guess from a friend who likes frogs 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
quests.hint: Pick the source written by someone who studied the topic.
quests.explanation: Books written by experts are more reliable than guesses or rumors.
quests.funFact: Good projects usually list where their information came from.

quests.instruction: What is one good thing about group work?
quests.correctAnswer: You can share ideas and skills 💡
options: You don't need to do anything 😴
You can share ideas and skills 💡
Only one person gets to talk 🗣️
quests.hint: Think about what several people can do together.
quests.explanation: Group members bring different ideas and strengths to make the project better.
quests.funFact: Ants and bees work in groups to do jobs that one animal alone could not.

quests.instruction: Your group is making a poster. Which job could one member do?
quests.correctAnswer: Draw the title 🖍️
options: Draw the title 🖍️
Take the poster home alone 🎒
Do everything for the group 🦸
quests.hint: Split the tasks.
quests.explanation: Sharing tasks lets each person focus on something they can do well.
quests.funFact: In a rowing boat with eight rowers, everyone must pull in time to go fast.

quests.instruction: What shows your group that you are listening?
quests.correctAnswer: Looking at the person speaking and nodding 👀
options: Looking out of the window at the field 🪟
Starting a side conversation with a friend 💬
Looking at the person speaking and nodding 👀
quests.hint: Listening includes body language.
quests.explanation: Looking and nodding show you are paying attention and value what they say.
quests.funFact: In many cultures looking at the speaker is a sign of respect, though customs differ.
